data.why: The app ships a built-in demo spectrum generator (Good/Marginal/Bad presets) enabled by default in the sidebar, which is the primary way to exercise the tool; two additional CSV files matching the app's wavenumber,intensity upload format were written for testing the file-upload path, one clean high-SNR spectrum and one with a dominant fluorescence background, baseline drift and a malformed row to exercise the quality-flagging and parser-robustness paths.

goals: Load the built-in demo spectrum and compare Confidence Scores across Good, Marginal and Bad quality presets
Upload a measured spectrum (CSV/TXT) and get an overall Confidence Score (0-100) with a letter grade
Inspect the per-metric breakdown (SNR, baseline stability, peak reproducibility, resolution, fluorescence contamination, hotspot uniformity) to see which metric is driving a low score
Visually compare the raw spectrum against its estimated baseline to judge whether baseline correction looks sensible
Decide whether a spectrum is trustworthy enough to keep in a dataset or should be re-measured
Download a text QC report summarizing the score and metric breakdown for record-keeping

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose (single-spectrum QC to decide keep vs re-measure) with sensible phases, covers everything the Streamlit app exposes, and reports its failures honestly, all checked against the screens. It needs fixes before filing: the bar-colour claim is wrong, two evidence citations are weak, check.json's screen IDs don't match the folder, and the missing keep/re-measure step and the uncertainty gap need to be stated clearly.
